title: Illinois midterm elections 2026: 3 key statewide and Chicago races to watch as candidates make final push for votes
text:
2026 election news: Suburban Cook County early voting turnout for midterms rises ahead of Illinois Election day - ABC7 Chicago 
 24/7 Live Chicago & Suburban Cook Co. North Suburbs West Suburbs South Suburbs NW Indiana Midterm Elections 
 Early voting turnout rises in Chicago, suburban Cook County ahead of Election Day 
 Early voting numbers point to increased voter turnout in suburban Cook County. WLS By Karen Jordan , Lissette Nuñez Monday, November 2, 2026 10:26PM Share Follow ABC7 on Google CHICAGO (WLS) -- Early voting numbers point to increased voter turnout in suburban Cook County, with more people casting ballots ahead of Election Day than at the same point during the 2022 midterm election.
 At the Bucktown-Wicker Park Library in Chicago, long lines of voters reflected the interest surrounding this year's midterm election. Some voters said the political climate and local races were motivating them to participate.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 Kathleen Maloney waited about 45 minutes in line before reaching the polling location. She said more people appear to be affected by the political climate.
 "I think everything going on in the country is truly driving everybody to want to get out and feel heard," Maloney said.
 Mitch Looman, who has voted at the location before, said he expected long lines. He has been paying close attention to races that could directly affect his community, including local school board elections.
 READ MORE | 2026 midterm elections: Voter information in Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin 
 "I think there's been a lot of attention about school board elections, and I think local elections that don't get a lot of news coverage still impact our lives a lot," Looman said.
 Joanna Williams is also following the school board race. She brought her dog, Andy, along while casting her ballot.
 "Hopefully it means we get a great turnout and good candidates in office," Williams said.

 "I wanted to make sure that I could vote and I wanted to avoid the lines tomorrow," Jean Osberger said. "Just wanted to make sure nothing would get in the way."
 The increased interest in early voting is also reflected in suburban Cook County's voting numbers.
 SEE ALSO | Illinois Early Voting Ballot Tracker 
 Cook County Clerk Monica Gordon said in-person and mail-in voting have increased 27% compared with the same point in the 2022 midterm election. As of the morning of the announcement, more than 242,000 residents had cast early ballots.
 "As of this morning, more than 242,000 residents have cast ballots in early voting," Gordon said.
 Gordon also cast her ballot on the final day of early voting. Looking ahead to Election Day, she said voters should feel safe when heading to the polls.
 More than 6,500 election judges across Cook County have received instructions on how to handle potential disruptions at polling places, according to Gordon.
 "Let me be very clear: No voter should ever feel intimidated, threatened or discouraged from exercising their right to vote," she said.
 Early voting ends at 7 p.m. Mail-in ballots submitted on time can be counted up to two weeks after Election Day.
